rubric: Identify NH₂/COOH versus C=C monomer features.
Describe peptide C–N joining versus a carbon backbone from addition.
State water release in the supplied condensation and no small-molecule release in ethene addition.
tasks.explanation: Amino acids have amino and acid functional groups and make peptide C–N links while releasing water at each actual junction. Ethene addition uses C=C monomers, makes a single carbon backbone and releases no small molecule.
tasks.hint: Compare both monomer groups and the products.

tasks.purpose: Higher: count the whole amino group
tasks.prompt: Given Ar N 14 and H 1, what is the relative mass of NH₂?
tasks.explanation: 14 + 2 × 1 = 16. Both H atoms belong to the original amino group.

tasks.title: Higher: count the whole acid group
tasks.purpose: Higher: count the whole acid group
tasks.prompt: Given Ar C 12, O 16 and H 1, what is the relative mass of COOH?
tasks.explanation: 12 + 2 × 16 + 1 = 45. COOH contains two oxygens.
tasks.hint: Count the carbonyl O and OH oxygen.

tasks.title: Higher: sum the unchanged groups
tasks.prompt: In H₂N–[unknown section]–COOH, NH₂ has relative mass 16 and COOH has relative mass 45. What is their combined contribution?
tasks.explanation: 16 + 45 = 61. The unknown middle section is not part of this total.
tasks.hint: Add the two printed end groups.

tasks.title: Higher: subtract a missing section
tasks.prompt: H₂N–[unknown section]–COOH has Mr 75. The unchanged NH₂ and COOH contribute 61. Find the unknown section’s relative mass.
tasks.explanation: 75 − 61 = 14. Do not replace the unknown section with a named molecule.

tasks.title: Higher: transfer the inverse calculation
tasks.prompt: An unfamiliar H₂N–[unknown section]–COOH monomer has Mr 103. Given Ar H 1, C 12, N 14, O 16, find its unknown section’s relative mass.
tasks.explanation: NH₂ contributes 16; COOH contributes 45. 103 − 61 = 42. This numerical mass alone does not identify a unique structure.
tasks.hint: Find the known end groups before subtracting.
